title: Comparing two quantities by percentage
summary: Calculate percentage increase or decrease between two quantities by measuring the difference against the stated reference quantity.
objectives: Find the absolute difference between two quantities.
Choose the original or stated comparison quantity as the denominator.
Explain why reversing a percentage comparison usually changes the answer.

sections.title: Compare the change with the starting quantity

blocks.text: For ‘A is what percentage more than B?’, the difference is
and B is the reference. Use
. For ‘A is what percentage less than B?’, B is again the stated reference.

Percentage comparisons are directional. If 50 is 25% more than 40, then 40 is 20% less than 50 because the same difference of 10 is divided by a different reference. Read the words after ‘than’ to identify the denominator.

sections.title: Worked example: percentage more

prompt.text: A club has 54 members this year and had 45 members last year. By what percentage did membership increase?

content.text: Compare the increase with last year’s membership.

sections.verification_note: The increase is one fifth of the original membership, so 20% is reasonable.

sections.title: Worked example: reverse the comparison

prompt.text: A is 25% more than B. By what percentage is B less than A?

content.text: Choose a convenient value, such as B = 100. Then A = 125.
Compare the difference with A because B is being described relative to A.

sections.verification_note: The two percentages differ because their reference quantities are 100 and 125.

prompt.text: A price rises from $60 to $72. Find the percentage increase.

feedback.text: The increase is $12. Divide 12 by the original price of 60 and multiply by 100%.

blocks.text: Find the difference, identify the reference named by the comparison, divide the difference by that reference, and multiply by 100%. Check the direction before choosing the denominator.
